metadata.title: Catch a Package Hallucination Before It Becomes a Slopsquatting Attack

beats.narration_text: Claude imports requests_oauth_helper — a name that doesn't exist on PyPI today but might be squatted tomorrow with malicious code inside.

props.command: import requests_oauth_helper  # does this exist on PyPI?

beats.narration_text: Hallucinated package names appear across thousands of model outputs. Slopsquatting works by registering those names with malicious payloads. The scanner catches the risk at the import line before pip install runs.

items.label: Hallucinated names
items.sub: Same fake package names recur across thousands of model outputs.

items.label: Registered by attackers
items.sub: Slopsquatters claim the fakes on PyPI or npm with malicious payloads.

items.label: Caught at the import
items.sub: A scanner blocks the risk before pip install ever runs.

beats.narration_text: We ask Claude to write a package auditor that reads import statements from a file and checks each against the PyPI JSON API.

props.command:
Write package_auditor.py:
  parse imports from a Python file
  query pypi.org/pypi/{name}/json per package
  print EXISTS or HALLUCINATED
  flag any 404 as SLOPSQUATTING RISK

beats.narration_text: Claude writes the auditor using requests and the PyPI API. It extracts top-level package names only, handles both 'import X' and 'from X import Y', and prints a color-coded verdict per package.

props.title: package_auditor.py

beats.narration_text: Scanner run: requests — EXISTS. numpy — EXISTS. requests_oauth_helper — HALLUCINATED — 404. Slopsquatting risk flagged. The malicious payload would install on pip install without any warning.

props.title: scanner_run.txt
props.code:
$ python package_auditor.py app.py
requests:              EXISTS
numpy:                 EXISTS
requests_oauth_helper: HALLUCINATED <- SLOPSQUATTING RISK

# 404 from pypi.org = registry has no such package.
# pip install would happily fetch a squatted replacement.

beats.narration_text: We extend the scanner with a --npm flag for JavaScript imports using the npm registry API.

props.command:
Extend package_auditor.py with a --npm flag:
  read JS/TS require and import statements
  hit registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search?text=<pkg>
  same EXISTS / HALLUCINATED output

beats.narration_text: npm scan: react — EXISTS. lodash — EXISTS. react-query-optimizer-v3 — HALLUCINATED. The pattern is identical across ecosystems — any package name a model invents is a potential squatting target.

props.title: npm_scan.txt
props.code:
$ python package_auditor.py --npm ui.js
react:                     EXISTS       (200)
lodash:                    EXISTS       (200)
react-query-optimizer-v3:  HALLUCINATED (404) <- SLOPSQUATTING RISK

# Same failure mode on npm — invented names are squatting targets.

beats.narration_text: The hallucination rate is low but the recurrence rate is high — the same fake names appear across thousands of outputs. Scan imports before pip install, not after.
